title: Critique: the view slides back into epiphenomenalism

statements.text: If a conscious state is a high-level brain state with an experiential side, and all causation runs through the third-person side, the experience does no causal work. Then why it exists and how it evolved are unexplained, which is the epiphenomenalism Searle rejects.

sources.quote: Does not this approach just return us to the absurd epiphenomenalism that Searle has rejected so unequivocally?
